proposals.before: Xiao Aludai, whose courtesy name was Yixin, came from the Wuwei tribe.
proposals.after: Xiao Aludai, whose courtesy name was Yixinyin, came from the Wuwei tribe.
proposals.reason: Chinese courtesy name 乙辛隱 is three characters; English drops 隱 and should read Yixinyin.

proposals.before: Xiao Aludai, courtesy name Yixin, was a man of the Wuwei tribe.
proposals.after: Xiao Aludai, courtesy name Yixinyin, was a man of the Wuwei tribe.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise truncates 乙辛隱 to Yixin; restore Yixinyin.

proposals.before: In the third year of Qiantong, for keeping Song captives who should have been sent back as slaves, he was dismissed from office.
proposals.after: In the third year of Qiantong, for keeping as slaves Song captives who should have been sent back, he was dismissed from office.
proposals.reason: Chinese 當遣還者為奴 means captives who ought to be repatriated were kept as slaves; the literal reverses the relation.

proposals.before: During Shoulong he rose through several posts to tiyin and vice director, and was granted the title of meritous minister who preserves integrity.
proposals.after: During Shoulong he rose through several posts to tiyin and vice director, and was granted the title of meritorious minister who preserves integrity.

proposals.before: During Shoulong he was repeatedly promoted to Tiyin, concurrently Vice Director, and granted the title Meritous Minister who Preserves Integrity.
proposals.after: During Shoulong he was repeatedly promoted to Tiyin, concurrently Vice Director, and granted the title Meritorious Minister who Preserves Integrity.
proposals.reason: Same spelling error in the literal English field.

decisions.reason: 字乙辛隱 is a three-character courtesy name; idiomatic Yixin drops 隱, and Yixinyin restores the full romanization without changing the rest of the sentence.
Literal likewise truncates 乙辛隱 to Yixin; Yixinyin matches the Chinese courtesy name while preserving the rest of the wording.
坐留宋俘當遣還者為奴 means he kept as slaves Song captives who ought to have been repatriated; “sent back as slaves” misattaches 為奴 to the repatriation clause, and the proposed reordering fixes that relation.
保節功臣 is rendered meritorious minister who preserves integrity; idiomatic meritous is a misspelling of meritorious and does not change the Chinese honorific.
Literal Meritous is the same misspelling of Meritorious for 保節功臣; correcting the spelling restores the standard English rendering of 功臣.
